title: Clean Palindrome
statement:
A text is a **clean palindrome** if it reads the same forwards and backwards after you ignore everything that is not a letter or a digit, and ignore upper/lower case.

Return `true` if `text` is a clean palindrome, otherwise `false`. A text with no letters or digits at all counts as a clean palindrome.
constraints: text contains printable ASCII characters only

args: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
examples.explanation: Ignoring symbols, spaces and case this is amanaplanacanalpanama, which is a palindrome.

hints.nudge: Which characters actually matter? Try crossing out the ones that do not in the first example.
hints.pattern: Two pointers: compare characters from both ends moving toward the middle.
hints.pseudocode:
i = 0; j = len-1
while i < j:
  if text[i] is not a letter/digit: i++
  else if text[j] is not a letter/digit: j--
  else if lower(text[i]) != lower(text[j]): return false
  else: i++; j--
return true
hints.walkthrough: Building a cleaned copy and comparing it with its reverse works in O(n) time but uses O(n) extra space. With two pointers you skip symbols in place: move i right past non-alphanumeric characters, move j left past them, then compare the two characters ignoring case. If they ever differ the answer is false; if the pointers meet, it is true.
